approach: Static recompilation of the guest x86 to C, compiled natively for x86-64, with a software NV2A push-buffer executor in place of the GPU
help: Stage world rendering: fixed-function batches and texture binding
GL back end: the stage's ground mesh is discarded on fragment alpha

Save file: location, format and persistence across runs
notes: As of 2026-11-02: the start-game stage draws its world -- bamboo, haze, light shafts, water and the player's model -- on both back ends. The ground is still missing, and the fault is now localised to the OpenGL back end: the 960-vertex ground mesh is submitted, covers the pixel, and is dropped by the fragment alpha, since RECOMP_GL_ALPHA_ONE paints it. The CPU rasteriser samples the same decoded texture and paints the same pixel, so the two back ends disagree about one combiner, not about the data. The MSVC 2022 build is verified end to end (build, boot, input, XAudio2) with one clock_gettime guard in the toolkit. As of 2026-10-25: boots the retail USA XBE, runs the title's own main loop, plays the attract video and streams the menu BGM. With a physical gamepad (RECOMP_USB=1), repeated maintainer runs reach New Game, save creation and loading, the main menu, the start-game stage and the pause menu. On the start-game stage the player's 3D model is drawn, but the stage world is not: only bamboo is visible. Next: stage world rendering. A black screen after New Game was seen in two runs on 2026-10-24, neither with RECOMP_AC97_READY=1; later runs with it did not show it. The cause is not established. Static recompilation with a pinned xboxrecomp submodule; no emulator and no CPU interpreter. The DSP is a passthrough stub, so audio effects are absent. The MinGW-w64 Windows cross-build is verified to link and reach the display-mode call under Wine; the MSVC 2022 path builds and boots with Visual Studio Build Tools 2022, MSVC 19.44 and Windows SDK 10.0.26100. Needs your own legally obtained USA Xbox disc; no game data is included.
